comparison: Perfect agreement on epitope identification and escape mapping (C24-C28). Both evaluations find these claims supported. OpenEval notes methodological limitations acknowledged in C94-C95, while peer reviewers praised the application of well-established approaches from HIV research.

Strong agreement on fitness decline during early infection (C35-C39, C43-C44). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes reliance on assumptions about sequence prevalence reflecting fitness, while peer reviewers explicitly accepted the correlational evidence without critique. OpenEval includes C83 which peer reviewers address separately in R8.

Agreement on temporal dynamics showing non-significant correlations post-90 DPI (C40-C42, C45). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes the interpretation involves inference and potential statistical power issues, while peer reviewers implicitly accepted this as part of the fitness rebound narrative. Peer R5 also includes C46 which OpenEval addresses in R11.

Agreement on study cohort characteristics (C19-C23). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes clear documentation in Table 1, while peer reviewers praised the longitudinal design with frequent sampling. OpenEval includes C98-C99 which peer reviewers do not separately address.

Partial overlap on correlation findings (C29-C30). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=14 epitopes) as a limitation, while peer reviewers accepted the correlational findings as part of overall evidence. Peer R3 also covers C31-C34 which OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Agreement on temporal correlations pre- and post-90 DPI (C31-C34). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes the interpretation involves inferring causality from correlation, while peer reviewers accepted the temporal distinction as part of the convincing study design.

Agreement on detailed haplotype and fitness analysis (C50-C56). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval emphasizes the internal consistency and strong evidence for epistatic interactions, while peer reviewers highlighted the focus on co-occurring mutations as a major strength. Peer R6 covers a broader set of fitness rebound claims.

Agreement on fitness rebound observations in two subjects (C47-C49). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes this sets up detailed analysis, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the overall fitness rebound narrative. Peer R6 covers the full fitness rebound analysis including compensatory mutations.

Agreement on fitness restoration through co-occurring mutations in second subject (C57-C58). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval emphasizes generalizability while highlighting individual variation, peer reviewers accepted this as part of the comprehensive fitness rebound findings.

Agreement on reversion mutations and fitness restoration (C59-C60). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes the assumption that consensus sequences represent optimal fitness, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the compensatory mutation analysis.

Agreement on synthesis of epistasis findings (C61-C62, C88-C90). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes limited generalization due to small number of subjects showing fitness rebound (2 of 6), while peer reviewers accepted these as main conclusions. Peer R6 covers broader fitness rebound findings, while OpenEval R15 also addresses C90 covered in peer R8.

Agreement on timing comparisons between clearers and chronic progressors (C66-C68). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes limited statistical power for clearers (n=3), while peer reviewers accepted the temporal relationships as part of convincing overall study. Peer R7 covers broader immune response timing claims.

Agreement on temporal associations and immune dominance transition (C69-C71). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes the interpretation is inferential and pattern not consistent across all subjects, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the temporal relationship between immune responses and outcomes.

Agreement on temporal associations in subject with two T/F viruses (C72-C73). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes the interpretation of nAb ineffectiveness is inferential and dual T/F infection may complicate interpretation, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of overall immune response timing narrative.

Agreement on main conclusions integrating immune timing with outcomes (C74, C91-C92). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes causality cannot be definitively established from observational data, while peer reviewers accepted the temporal relationships as showing the progression mechanism.

Agreement on comparative context from other viral systems (C84-C85). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes these provide comparative framing, while peer reviewers praised the application of HIV research approaches to HCV as lending rigor. Peer R8 covers broader integrative approach claims.

Agreement on literature gaps establishing study rationale (C86-C87). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes these establish novelty, while peer reviewers accepted the integrative approach as filling these gaps. Peer R8 covers broader methodological integration claims.

Agreement on confirmatory observation (C93). Both evaluations support this claim. OpenEval notes this confirms previous work, while peer reviewers accepted this as part of the comprehensive integration of findings.

Agreement on computational approach limitations (C94-C95). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes appropriate scientific caution, while peer reviewers stated limitations were clearly identified after revision. Peer R9 also covers vaccine implications (C96-C97).

Divergence on speculative implications (C96-C97, C100). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they represent extrapolation beyond the data without direct evidence testing vaccine hypotheses. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting vaccine implications as appropriate contribution to understanding HCV evolution.
